item.title: Hegseth is said to have summoned US military brass from across globe
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has called an unprecedented meeting of generals and admirals at a Marine Corps base in Virginia next week, raising concerns within the military. The reason for the gathering remains undisclosed, fueling anxiety amidst recent firings of senior officers, including women and people of colour.

item.title: 'Palestinians won't leave Gaza,' Abbas tells UN via video
item.description: Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas condemned Israel's actions in Gaza as war crimes during his UN General Assembly address. Speaking remotely from Ramallah due to denied US visas, Abbas denounced the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, emphasizing it doesn't represent the Palestinian people.

item.title: ‘Trump orders probe into violent protest funding; justice dept to target Soros-backed groups
item.description: President Trump has directed federal agencies to investigate the financial backers of groups accused of funding violent protests, specifically naming George Soros and Reid Hoffman. The Justice Department is preparing investigative plans targeting groups funded by Soros, citing potential charges like racketeering and material support for terrorism.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Zelenskyy to UN: Stop Russia's war now or face destructive arms race
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged world powers to unite against Russia's aggression, warning that Putin aims to expand the conflict beyond Ukraine. He highlighted airspace violations in Poland and Estonia as evidence of Russia testing boundaries.

item.title: ‘A real war’: Russian FM Lavrov blames EU, NATO for Ukraine conflict; cites direct role
item.description: Sergey Lavrov accused NATO and the EU of waging a "real war" against Russia through Ukraine, during a G20 meeting. Britain dismissed Lavrov's claims as distortions, while tensions escalate due to Russian airspace incursions into Poland, Romania, and Estonia. NORAD also intercepted Russian military aircraft near Alaska, amid ongoing conflict in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump approves TikTok deal, Xi gives go-ahead to US ownership
item.description: Donald Trump signed an executive order finalizing a deal allowing TikTok to operate in the US, with a majority stake moving to US investors like Oracle and Silver Lake. ByteDance will retain less than 20% equity. Much is still unknown about the actual arrangement, but Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping “gave us the go-ahead” to proceed with the deal.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Goody bag of unnecessary pills: Indian-origin Dr Neil K Anand, who treated 9/11 patients, sentenced to 14 years in prison
item.description: Dr Anand and his family disputed the allegations and said his compassion for his patients was fairly criminalized. They said Dr Anand went to ground zero on the day of 9/11 attack when he was an intern and treated patients. "The government is using artificial intelligence and manipulated data to prosecute me for treating chronic pain patients, turning tools meant to help into weapons against doctors," Dr Anand said earlier.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pak PM Shehbaz Sharif meets Sri Lanka president & Yunus in New York
item.description: On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly's 80th session in New York, PM Shehbaz Sharif engaged in discussions with Bangladesh's chief adviser, Muhammad Yunus, focusing on strengthening bilateral ties through trade, connectivity, and cultural exchange. Sharif also met with Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, addressing high-level exchanges, trade, education, culture, and defense cooperation to enhance their relationship.

item.title: ‘It was just me’: Dallas shooter hated US government, aimed to terrorize federal agents; ‘specific intentions’ revealed
item.description: A gunman, identified as Joshua Jahn, launched a targeted attack on an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility in Dallas, resulting in one detainee's death and two injuries. Jahn, who fatally shot himself, harbored deep animosity towards the US government and ICE agents, aiming to incite terror.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Deeply distressing’: Hackers claim data theft of 8,000 children from Kido Nurseries in London, India, US, and China; demand ransom
item.description: Cybercriminals have reportedly stolen sensitive data, including names, pictures, and addresses of approximately 8,000 children from the Kido nursery chain, which operates in London, India, China, and the US. The hackers are demanding a ransom, using the stolen data, which also includes information about parents and safeguarding notes.

item.title: Man arrested for Oldbury rape gets bail, sparking anger in Sikh community
item.description: A British Sikh woman was racially motivated raped in Oldbury, leading to community outrage after the arrested suspect was released on bail. Crimestoppers and the Sikh community are offering rewards for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the two white men involved.
item.dc:creator: NAOMI CANTON

item.title: ‘Scrambling to change plans’: Pentagon summons top military leaders to rare in-person meeting in Virginia; purpose not revealed
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has called for a rare, in-person meeting of top U.S. military leaders at Quantico, Virginia, causing widespread disruption. The purpose of the gathering remains unclear, but it involves senior officers globally, raising questions about its urgency and necessity.

item.title: ‘Woman in pink’: Russian national’s body identified in Spain after 20 years; police suspect foul play
item.description: In a significant breakthrough, Interpol has identified Liudmila Zavada as the "Woman in Pink," whose body was discovered in Spain in 2005. The identification, made possible through Interpol's 'Identify Me' campaign, involved matching fingerprints from Turkish police with Zavada's DNA.

item.title: Airspace violation: Norad scrambles jets to intercept Russian bombers near Alaska; claims activity ‘occurs regularly’
item.description: NORAD scrambled fighter jets to intercept Russian military aircraft near Alaska, which remained in international airspace and posed no threat. This activity is routine in the Alaskan Air Defense Identification Zone. The announcement follows accusations of Russian airspace violations in Estonia and Poland, with President Trump suggesting NATO countries should shoot down violating planes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump-Erdogan meeting: US prez asks Turkey to stop buying Russian oil; F-35 jet deal on agenda
item.description: During a meeting in the Oval Office, President Trump urged Turkish President Erdogan to halt Russian oil purchases, aiming to pressure Moscow to end the conflict in Ukraine. Trump expressed readiness for major sanctions on Russia if all NATO nations ceased buying Russian oil.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Most powerful AI’: Trump, Elon Musk come together once again after Charlie Kirk funeral
item.description: The Trump administration's GSA has partnered with Elon Musk's xAI, offering federal agencies access to Grok AI chatbots at a nominal fee. Musk stated this will drive innovation while keeping costs low. Agencies will pay just 42 cents for 18 months of access, with support from xAI engineers.
